title: V01-C15 Scope, Lifetime, and Side Effects Production Packet
required_components: Global Module Function and Block Scope

assessment_alignment.acceptance_evidence: A lexical-scope diagram and identifier-resolution trace that distinguishes global, module, function, and block bindings; explains shadowing without calling it reassignment; and separates accessibility from lifetime.
An effect inventory and before-after design that moves hidden state, clock, randomness, console, or mutation behind explicit inputs and an effect boundary while preserving behavior with tests.

accessibility_requirements: Scope diagrams include numbered text lookup traces.
Lifetime timelines distinguish binding visibility, object reachability, and collection uncertainty.
Effect diagrams label reads, writes, returned values, and external boundaries.
Turkish terms include English only at first meaningful use.
Code comments and explanations are Turkish.
known_risks: Scope and lifetime may be conflated.
Dynamic call order may be mistaken for lexical resolution.
Shadowing may be described as mutation.
Closure capture may be described as copying.
End of scope may be equated with immediate garbage collection.
Console output may be confused with returned output.
Purity may be presented as elimination of all useful effects.
Local mutation may be classified without checking observability.
